title: AffineDriftPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Nonconvex objectives are permitted: global PL and L-Lipschitz gradient are required, but convexity is not.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objective with an attained global minimum and global PL inequality 2μ(f(x)−f(xstar)) ≤ ‖∇f(x)‖². The initial objective gap is at most Δ.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each sequential call k queries x and returns the scalar f(x)+a(q)+b(q)r+e(k,x), where q=⌊k/(d+2)⌋ and r=k mod (d+2). The reply is independent of the oracle seed. All scalar calls count toward the fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Residual function-value errors satisfy |e(k,x)| ≤ ν uniformly over calls and points, without unbiasedness, independence, or stochastic moment assumptions. Valid parameters obey 4dLν ≤ με.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: spec.admissible residual bound and spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: affine_drift
distinctive_assumptions.details: Unknown arbitrary intercept a(q) and slope b(q) within each aligned block of d+2 sequential calls. Neither coefficient is bounded, and both can change arbitrarily between blocks.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: spec.admissible, existential a, b, e.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain, queries, and output lie in d-dimensional real Euclidean space, with d>0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ZerothOrderSmoothAndConvex.lean: ZerothOrder.Point; LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: spec.Instance, spec.Query, spec.Output, spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, with 0<μ≤L and ε>0. Public algorithm inputs are d, L, μ, ε, and x0; Δ≥0 and ν≥0 are hidden parameters. Drift coefficients and residual errors are not supplied to the algorithm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a single point whose latent objective gap satisfies f(output)−f(xstar) ≤ ε for a global minimizer xstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the execution probability law. Oracle cost is bounded for every seed by the fixed budget ⌈(L/μ)log(1+2Δ/ε)⌉(d+2).
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineDriftPL.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence; supplied extracted budget for OracleTemplate.AffineDriftPL.result.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth PL minimization uses a sequential function-value oracle with arbitrary blockwise affine temporal drift and uniformly bounded residual errors constrained by the target accuracy. This structured observation model is an unusual variant of standard zeroth-order optimization.

descriptionHtml:
PL Minimization with Affine Drift

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥1. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, and it satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with constant 0<μ≤L. A given point x0 has objective gap at most Δ≥0 from a global minimizer x⋆. The oracle returns function values corrupted by arbitrary affine drift within blocks of d+2 calls and deterministic errors bounded by ν≥0. For ε>0 with 4dLν≤με, the goal is an output x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x), where d is an integer and ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives only d,L,μ,ε, and x0; the parameters Δ and ν may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f is differentiable everywhere, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality and initial gap). There exists x⋆∈Rd such that f(x⋆)≤f(x),x∈Rd,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ,2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2,x∈Rd.

Assumption 3 (Blockwise affine oracle drift). There are fixed real sequences (aj)j≥0 and (bj)j≥0 and fixed functions ek:Rd→R satisfying |ek(x)|≤ν,k≥0,x∈Rd. Index oracle calls from zero. On call k, a query at any x∈Rd returns the scalar yk(x)=f(x)+aj+bjr+ek(x),j=⌊kd+2⌋,r=k−j(d+2)∈{0,…,d+1}. The intercepts aj and slopes bj are arbitrary and may differ between blocks.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈Rd must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

budget.value: fun p => ⌈p.L / p.μ * Real.log (1 + 2 * p.Δ / p.ε)⌉₊ * (p.d + 2)

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rd→R, d≥1, has an L-Lipschitz gradient and a global minimizer x⋆, with 0<μ≤L, 2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2, and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ. Query k returns f(x)+at+btj+ek(x), where t=⌊k/(d+2)⌋, j=kmod(d+2), at,bt are arbitrary, and |ek(x)|≤ν. Assume Δ,ν≥0, ε>0, and 4dLν≤με. Target: f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under the oracle law; the constructed deterministic method satisfies it for every outcome.

Value-oracle optimization with aligned affine drift: AffineDriftPL.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) DriftCorrectedGD (Ours) (review) O(d[1+Lμlog⁡(1+Δε)]) value calls.
(2) Forward-difference GD, derived bound (Berahas et al. 2022; Friedlander and Schmidt 2012); Thm. 2.1 and the PL form of Lemma 2.1 O(d[1+Lμlog⁡(1+Δε)]) value calls. Special case: at=bt=0; 4dLν≤με. (1): Matches known rate; formalizes the PL guarantee. Scope: permits arbitrary affine drift within exactly aligned (d+2)-query blocks. (1): One extra value query per iteration, including on the drift-free restriction.
(3) TOBYQA (Yao and Xie 2026), v2, §3.2, affine-drift invariance Gradient-recovery guarantee for f(x)+βk+ek(x); full-rank augmented interpolation matrix. No objective-gap budget. (1): Scope extends global affine drift to arbitrary jumps between aligned blocks; affine-drift cancellation itself is already known.
(4) TOBYQA (Yao and Xie 2026), v2, §4.4, expected stationarity Expected hitting time for ∥∇f(x)∥≤τ for τ≥Cκegmax{δhi,σ/δlo}. Assumes probabilistically fully-linear models, bounded sample radii, controlled acceptance bias, sub-Gaussian innovations, and regularization confinement. Rates not comparable. (1): Deterministic objective-gap guarantee under PL, instead of expected stationarity; no identical-output speedup asserted. (1): Needs PL and 4dLν≤με; no coverage of general nonconvex objectives or C2 nonlinear drift with controlled residual bias.

Abbr: PL: Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality; d: dimension; L: gradient Lipschitz constant; μ: PL constant; Δ: initial objective-gap bound; ν: value-error bound; ε: objective accuracy; K: iteration count; τ: gradient-norm tolerance; β: global drift slope. Costs count individual value queries. In (4), δlo,δhi bound sample radii, σ is the noise scale, κeg is the model-error constant, and C is universal.

Berahas, Albert S., Liyuan Cao, Krzysztof Choromanski, and Katya Scheinberg. 2022. “A Theoretical and Empirical Comparison of Gradient Approximations in Derivative-Free Optimization.” Foundations of Computational Mathematics 22 (2): 507–60. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10208-021-09513-z.
Friedlander, Michael P., and Mark Schmidt. 2012. “Hybrid Deterministic-Stochastic Methods for Data Fitting.” SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 34 (3): A1380–405. https://doi.org/10.1137/110830629.
Yao, Haoyu, and Pengcheng Xie. 2026. TOBYQA: A Time-Augmented Model-Based Method for Derivative-Free Optimization Under Noise and Temporal Drift. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.18124.

import LongTails.Setups.ZerothOrderSmoothAndConvex

namespace LongTails.Setups.AffineDriftPL

open OracleTemplate

open LongTails.Setups.ZerothOrderSmoothAndConvex

structure Public where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : Point d

structure Params extends Public where
  Δ : ℝ
  ν : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := Point p.d → ℝ
  Query p := Point p.d
  Reply _ := ℝ
  Output p := Point p.d
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.d ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.ν ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    4 * (p.d : ℝ) * p.L * p.ν ≤ p.μ * p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ (a b : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → Point p.d → ℝ), (∀ k x, |e k x| ≤ p.ν) ∧
      ∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = f x + a (k.length / (p.d + 2)) +
        b (k.length / (p.d + 2)) * (k.length % (p.d + 2) : ℕ) + e k.length x) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ ∧
      ∀ x, 2 * p.μ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2)
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.AffineDriftPL
